---
title: "API map"
description: "Find a public class or function by task."
---

Most code starts with one of three modules:

```python
from pypanelsim import core, designs, primitives
```

Root-level imports also work. The documentation keeps the module name because
it shows what each object does.

## By task

| Task | Start with | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Define dimensions and compose a simulation | `core.PanelSimulator` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Inspect arrays, identifiers, annotations, and known effects | `core.PanelDataset` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Make randomness stable by component | `core.SimulationSeeds` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Choose a feature or assignment model | `primitives` | [Building blocks](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Choose an untreated-outcome model | `primitives` | [Building blocks](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Choose a treatment-effect model | `primitives` | [Building blocks](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Run a ready-made design | `designs` | [Designs](reference/designs.qmd) |
| Register local design factories | `core.DGPRegistry` | [Registry](reference/registry.qmd) |

## Constructor and direct-draw convention

Ready-made families use two related functions:

```python
simulator = designs.baker_design()
panel = designs.baker(seed=42)
```

The `_design` function returns a reusable `PanelSimulator`. The shorter function
runs one draw and returns a `PanelDataset`.

## Supported imports

`core`, `primitives`, and `designs` form the documented public API. Objects
imported from internal modules can change. Public names follow the package's
release and deprecation policy.

## Error conventions

Constructors validate configuration values at creation. Simulation validates
drawn matrix shapes, finite values, binary treatment, and the causal identity.
Errors identify the failed field or component. A component should not silently
turn an invalid probability model into a valid one.
